mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the federal funds rate over 3 consecutive months indicates the Federal Reserve is shifting to an easing stance, lowering discount rates and increasing equity present value, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 4% signals tightening monetary policy, raising discount rates and compressing equity present value, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in tightening periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) exceeding 5% month-over-month suggests weak labor demand, lowering consumer spending and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns in rising claims periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) below 2% month-over-month signals strengthening labor demand, boosting consumer confidence and corporate profits, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in falling claims periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Industrial Production index above 2% indicates expanding domestic production capacity, which lowers marginal costs and supports higher corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in rising production periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in retail sales (HOUST) exceeding 3% indicates weakening consumer demand, compressing corporate margins and reducing equity valuations, which predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in declining sales periods are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in retail sales (HOUST) above 4% month-over-month signals strong consumer demand, boosting corporate profits and equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns in rising sales periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 2% over 3 months indicates disinflation, lowering inflation risk premiums and supporting equity valuations, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in disinflation periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05), or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
